# Lab 13.10: AI.FORECAST & AI.DETECT_ANOMALIES with TimesFM

## What We Are Going to Do
Forecast bike trips and detect anomalies with the pre-trained TimesFM model, with no model training at all.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Forecast 14 days for 5 stations.** Uses `lab12.daily_trips` from Lab 12.10.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT id AS station, forecast_timestamp, ROUND(forecast_value) AS forecast,
       ROUND(prediction_interval_lower_bound) AS low, ROUND(prediction_interval_upper_bound) AS high
FROM AI.FORECAST(
  TABLE lab12.daily_trips,
  data_col =&gt; 'trips',
  timestamp_col =&gt; 'day',
  id_cols =&gt; ['station'],
  horizon =&gt; 14,
  confidence_level =&gt; 0.9
)
ORDER BY station, forecast_timestamp;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Compare with the ARIMA_PLUS forecast from Lab 12.10. TimesFM needed no `CREATE MODEL`.

2. **[SQL] Detect anomalies in recent days.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT *
FROM AI.DETECT_ANOMALIES(
  (SELECT * FROM lab12.daily_trips WHERE day &lt; DATE_SUB((SELECT MAX(day) FROM lab12.daily_trips), INTERVAL 30 DAY)),
  (SELECT * FROM lab12.daily_trips WHERE day &gt;= DATE_SUB((SELECT MAX(day) FROM lab12.daily_trips), INTERVAL 30 DAY)),
  data_col =&gt; 'trips',
  timestamp_col =&gt; 'day',
  id_cols =&gt; ['station'],
  anomaly_prob_threshold =&gt; 0.95
)
WHERE is_anomaly;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The first query is history; the second is the period to check.

3. **[Console] Chart history and forecast.** Union the history from `lab12.daily_trips` with the forecast and open the results **Chart** tab.

4. **[CLI] Forecast from bq.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false \
"SELECT forecast_timestamp, forecast_value FROM AI.FORECAST(
   (SELECT day, SUM(trips) AS trips FROM lab12.daily_trips GROUP BY day),
   data_col =&gt; 'trips', timestamp_col =&gt; 'day', horizon =&gt; 7)"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Training | None, TimesFM is pre-trained |
| `AI.FORECAST` | Values with prediction intervals |
| `AI.DETECT_ANOMALIES` | Flags unusual recent days |
| Many series | `id_cols` |
